text:
A: Hello. I'm Nusrat.
B: Hiya. Leanne.
A: Where are you?
B: Whittlesey. It's near Peterborough.
A: I'm in Ilford. East London.
B: Right.
A: Your shelves are very well labelled. Is that work?
B: Erm, yeah. I do the office for my dad's plumbing and heating firm. Invoicing, the books, VAT, booking jobs in. They're all the old years.
A: Do you keep paper copies as well as the software?
B: Yeah. My dad doesn't trust it otherwise. We're on Xero now, but he likes to see a file.
A: That's sensible. I'm a management accountant at a housing association. We use Oracle, and the paper still turns up anyway, from the budget holders.
B: Oh, so you do accounts properly then. I've only got AAT.
A: AAT is proper. Half the people I work with couldn't do a VAT return.
B: Yeah? Well, that's good to know. Do you do much of that?
A: Not VAT, no. I do variance reports for repairs and maintenance. Mainly I'm chasing managers who send their figures late, or send them roughly. I don't accept roughly.
B: Erm, no, I'm the same with the engineers. They'll change a job round and not tell me, then I've invoiced the wrong customer. I do tell them.
A: You should. Otherwise it comes back on you.
B: Exactly. And customers who don't pay. Some of them are three months behind on a boiler service and act surprised when I ring.
A: What do you do after the reminder email?
B: I just phone them. Tell them straight, it's overdue, when are you paying. Most of them pay that week.
A: Good. People respond to a direct phone call.
B: Yeah. I don't really know what else to say about it.
A: That's fine.
B: Erm, is it a big team, where you are?
A: Quite big. I supervise one assistant. I have to remind her of the same deadlines every month.
B: Do you want to manage more people, then?
A: No. I'd rather be the expert than the boss.
B: Yeah, no, I get that. My dad wants me to take on more when he retires, and I'm a director already, on paper, but that's sort of just for tax.
A: On paper still counts. You know where every pound goes. That's most of running a small business.
B: Maybe. I'm not sure I could manage the engineers, to be fair.
A: You already tell them when they're wrong. That's managing.
B: Huh. I hadn't thought of it like that.
A: It's true, though. Do you have a deadline coming up?
B: VAT's due end of the month. I've nearly done it. What about you?
A: Month-end close next week. I'll be knackered.
B: I bet. Do you recheck everything?
A: Three times. Is that excessive?
B: No, I'd do the same, to be honest. Better than getting it...
